short: An elective monarchy over central Europe that lasted more than eight centuries.
full:
Otto I was crowned emperor in Rome on 2 February 962, reviving for the German kings the imperial title Charlemagne had taken in 800. It was never a state in the modern sense. An elected King of the Romans, crowned emperor by the pope, presided over several hundred duchies, bishoprics, free cities and knightly territories that made their own law and fought their own wars. The Golden Bull of 1356 fixed the electorate at seven, and from 1438 the Habsburgs held the title almost without a break.

The Reformation split it along confessional lines, and the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 confirmed the princes as effectively sovereign; Voltaire's remark that it was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire belongs to this long twilight. Napoleon finished it. After Austerlitz and the creation of the Confederation of the Rhine, Francis II laid down the crown on 6 August 1806, having taken the title Emperor of Austria two years earlier as insurance.
